## What is this?

DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`) is a command-line tool. For anyone who does not live in a
terminal, that me

ans installing Node, remembering commands, picking a port, and
cleaning up stray processes.
**DSH Ready is a small desktop window that does those seven things for you:**
| Thing | What happens |
| Install | Picks the version, checks your Node/npm, then installs DSH into npm's default global pre

fix — no sudo; a missing runtime gets an official download link |
| Start | Reads your login shell e

nvironment, starts `dsh web` on your port, opens it in your browser |
| Stop | Stops the process gro

up it started, or the external instance you asked it to take over |
| Status | Running / stopped / e

xternal instance / installing / upgrading, refreshed live |
| Logs | Live output panel plus an on-di

sk log, so failures are readable |
| Upgrade | Checks every third-party plugin against the target ve

rsion first, then upgrades DSH and the plugins |
| Uninstall | Stops, removes plugins, clears the pr
ofile, removes DSH — keeps `~/.dsh` and your npm setup |

It is deliberately **not** a plugin manager, not a MCP client, not a second DSH UI.
It starts the of
ficial web UI in your system browser.

> This is a community project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or maintained
> by DeepSeek.

The macOS builds carry an **ad-hoc signature**, so Apple Silicon accepts them without
a paid develop

er certificate. They are not notarized, so a freshly downloaded copy may
still be blocked once: open

**System Settings → Privacy & Security** and choose
**Open Anyway** (macOS 14 and older: right-clic

k the app → **Open**). If macOS claims the

`. On Windows, choose

All screenshots are captured from the real app running inside a sandbox, by

## How it works

- **System DSH first.** If `dsh` is already installed (npm global, Homebrew), the
launcher uses it i

nstead of installing a second copy. `dshSource` reports `system`
or `app` so the UI can say which on

e is live.
- **Login shell environment.** Apps launched from Finder inherit launchd's minimal
enviro

nment. DSH Ready runs `$SHELL -ilc 'env -0'` once and merges the result, so
API keys, proxies and `P

ATH` from `~/.zshrc` work exactly like in your terminal.
Skip it with `DSH_READY_SKIP_SHELL_ENV=1`.

- **One instance, one port.** It polls every 4 seconds for a `dsh web` listening on
the target port;

if something else runs there you can stop it or take it over.
DSH on other ports is never touched.

- **Upgrade plan before upgrade.** Plugin `peerDependencies` on `@deepseek-ai/dsh*`
and `engines.dsh

` are checked against the target version. A blocker is reported
and nothing is touched; only a passi

ng plan turns into executable commands.
- **Ports stay yours.** The default is 3080, edited in the s

ettings sheet (read-only in the
main window); a busy port is reported instead of silently shifted, s

o the address you see is real.
- **Settings in one place.** The header is four icons — language (文A)

, theme, settings, quit.
The settings sheet is grouped: general (launch at login, DSH port, open the

browser after
start, system tray icon, Dock icon on macOS, prevent idle sleep on macOS, theme, lang

uage),
network (npm registry auto/official/mirror, HTTP(S) proxy, extra DSH arguments) and privacy &

updates (anonymous launch report, daily check, manual check, plus a macOS-only system-permission
re

port that deep-links into Privacy & Security). The port is edited only there —
the main window shows

it read-only — and extra arguments go through an argv whitelist, never a
shell, with `--port` alway

s dropped. Sponsor entry at the bottom.
- **Your Node, your environment.** DSH Ready uses the Node a

nd npm from your login
shell. When Node is missing, older than 22.18, or has no npm, it does not mod

ify
your environment and shows the localized Node.js download page (Chinese UI → the

## Privacy

- The desktop app sends **nothing**. No telemetry, no update pings, no accounts.
- The website itsel

f collects **nothing** — no page-view counter, no cookies, no
third-party scripts. The only data on

this project's side is an anonymous launch
signal sent by the desktop app: a random device id, the U

TC date, the app version
and Cloudflare's coarse geo (country / region / city). No IP addresses, no

fingerprints, no user behaviour. The aggregates are public at
dsh.wordtk.com/stats.
